full_judgment:
The Government denied the aforesaid claim of the appellants by filling written statement on September 21, 1965 additional written statement on July 8, 1967 contending inter-alia that the entre land of R.S. plot No. 851 to which the suit lands are said to appertain  in have been leased to different card holders; and in the additional written statement, it was further contended that the suit lands are refermed lands of C.S.plots 6,7,12,20 and 21 of mouza kapal bera and card holders who have been impleaded as defendants 2 to 10 are in actual possession of the suit land. It was also contended that the suit lands were the new formation out of the bed of the river. 

 The suit was decreed by the subordinate judge in favour of the appellants. The Government preferred appeal to the High Court being First Appeal No. 524 of 1968 and corss-objection was filed by defendant respondents 2,4,5 and 8. A Division Bench of the High Court by the judgment and order dated December 7, 1976 allowed the appeal holding that the appeal including the suit abated in view of the provisions if the president’s order Nos. 135 and 137 of 1972. Against that order the appellants sought leave form this court on the contention that the High Court failed to notice that the amendments made to sections 86 and 87 of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 by the President’s order Nos. 135 and 137 of 1972, taking away the right of the tenants to the disuviated lands and to the reformation in situ and also the accretion thereto, having no retrospective operation to divest the tenants of their vested rights in the suit lands, the suit as framed was not affected by the said statutory provisions. Leave was granted to consider this question. 

 It is not disputed that the lands in question diluviated in the year 1351 B.S. corresponding to 1645 A.D. and after remaining under water for less than 20 years reappeared in 1357-58 B.S. corresponding to 1950-51 and the tenants entered into possession thereof, asserting their right to the land being reformation in situ and subsequent accretion thereto. The suit was filed or June 29, 1965. The written statement was filed by the Government on September 21, 1965. Additional written statement was filed by the Government on June 8, 1967 denying the claim of the appellants and alleging that the land lords were in actual physical possession of the suit lands and not the appellants as claimed in the suit. The suit was decreed on contest in favour of the appellants on August 30, 1967 and against the said decree the Government preferred on appeal to the High Court. From the judgment of the High Court it appears that the question of application to sections 86 and 87 of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 as mended by the Bangladesh state Acquisition and Tenancy (4th amendment) order 1972 (President’s order No. 135 of 1972 and the state Acquisition and Tenancy (6th amendment) order 1972 (President’s order No. 137 of 1972) to the suit has not been property considered. From the bar it was submitted that the plaintiffs right to the land having accrued in 1950-51 and their title having already been decreed by the civil court before the amendment, the suit was not affected by the amendments but the appeal preferred against the decree being pending, was effected, that is to say, the appeal abated, but not the suit. The learned Judges in rejecting the argument only observed that it is incompatible with the provisions of sections 86 and 87 of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act as amended by the President’s order Nos. 135 and 137 of 1972. It was not been considered as to whether the sections as amended are applicable to all accretions without any limitation or the amendments are applicable only to such accretions as contemplated in sub-sections (1) and (2) of Section 87. 

 Mr. M.H. Khondkar, the learned counsel for the appellants has rightly contended that the suit lands being reformation in situ and partly being accretion thereto formed prior to the publication of the Notification under Part V of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the amendments made in Section 86 and 87 of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act have no application. In this context the learned counsel referred to a decision of this Division in Civil Appeal No. 33 of 1976, Abdul Mannan Vs. Kulade Ranjan Mowali wherein sections 86 and 87 as amended have been construed, with reference to this decision the learned counsel submitted that the question of abatement of the suit and the appeal is required to be re-examined by the High Court in the light of the decision of this Court. 

 The suit in the above noted case was instituted in 1948 for a declaration of the plaintiffs right and interest in the suit lands as korsa tenants and for confirmation of their possession therein as well as for permanent injunction responding the defendants including the Government from interfering with their possession in any madher. The suit land appertaining to the plots in suit diluviated and after reformation in situ and after it became fit for possossion the owners of the Estate settled the same with the predecessors of the plaintiffs on the basis of a korsa kabuliyat dated 1st January 1331 B.S. corresponding to May, 1924. Rents of the said newly created jamas having fallen in arrear the landlords in execution of a decree obtained by them, purchased the same in auction and settled in 1344-45 B.S. with the predecessors of some of the plaintiffs on the basis of a kabuliyat. The rent receiving interest of the landlords having been acquired under the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the Government  stepped into the shoes of the previous landlords and the plaintiffs became tenants directly under the Government but some of the lands had been wrongly recorded in the name of the Government. This led to filing of the suit. The suit was contested by the Government and some of the defendants. The suit was renumbered as title suit No. 59 of 1954 when it was transferred to the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Barisal and thereafter on the creation of Potuakhali as District, the suit after transfer was registered as T.S. No. 146 of 1969. The suit was, however, withdrawn on 3.8.71 with permission to institute a fresh suit on the same cause of action. Title suit No. 3 of 1972 was there after filed on 24.1.1972 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Potuakhali inpursuance of the aforesaid permission. After amendment of Sections 86 and 87 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 an application for recording abatement of the suit was filed by the Government. The learned Sub-Judge by his order dated March, 24, 1973 recorded abatement of suit, which was affirmed by the High Court in revision. Against this order leave was granted to examine the question as to whether the Section 86 and 87 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as amended by the Presidents Order Nos. 72, 135 and 137 of 1972 could be applied to the suit in respect of the lands in suit. This question was answered in the negative on taking the view that the suit was not hit by the amended provisions of Sections 86 and 87. It has been held that sub-section (3) will have operation only in respect of such accretions as have been contemplated in sub-section (3) of Section 87 of the Act. It has been further held that the provisions of sub-sections (2) and (3) of Section 86 of the Act cannot be given any retrospective effect beyond the date of coming into force of Part V of the Act in the area in which the diluviated land is situated.
